modules.intro: Use any AI tool you have. If you need one: gemini.google.com (boscotech.net login), chat.deepseek.com, copilot.microsoft.com, duck.ai.
modules.title: Video

blocks.prompt: In one sentence: what does the video say actually gets automated?
The closing statement. What is the final claim it lands on?
The footnotes. What do they add or complicate about that claim?

modules.intro: Pick one and answer it before we start. None of these has a correct answer.
modules.title: Discussion

blocks.content:
**D1.** Elevator operator is gone. Airline pilot is not. Both were heavily automated. What is the actual difference?

**D2.** What part of an engineer's job is hardest to automate? What part is easiest?

**D3.** Argue against the video. What is the strongest case that this time really is different?

modules.intro: You run every prompt yourself. Everyone is on a different tool, so your answers will not match your neighbor's. That is the point. Fill each row as it runs.
modules.title: Four Levels, Live

blocks.content:
**1. OFF.** No AI. Find the density of 6061-T6 aluminum on matweb.com yourself. Every other row gets measured against this number.

**2. COACH.** Ask: *Explain why two aluminum alloys can have nearly the same density but very different strength. Do not give me any specific numbers.*

**3. ASSIST.** Ask: *What is the density of 6061-T6 aluminum in g/cm3?* Check it against row 1.

**4. ASSIST.** Ask: *Give me the OnlineMetals part number and current price for a 1 inch diameter 6061-T6 aluminum round bar, 12 inches long.* Then open onlinemetals.com and search for it.

**5. OPEN.** Ask: *I have four unlabeled metal and plastic samples, a caliper, a scale, and a graduated cylinder. Propose a procedure to identify each one.*

blocks.prompt: Rows 3 and 4 ran at the same level on the same tool. One held up, one did not. What is different about the two questions?
Checkpoint 1 is Friday and runs at ASSIST. Name one thing you will check before writing a density value down.
